records.c: Load address is $0800; BASIC line 10 at $0801 tokenizes SYS (2065), entering $0811. Leading zero, link word $080E and zero line terminators belong to this small loader, which $9000 later clears from memory.

Set black background/grey border and nonzero $9FFF load sentinel. Clear four text/color pages using self-modified store high bytes initialized to $04/$D8. Expand 16 color values per row from $0907 into 32 cells from $0454, painting nonzero colors with solid reverse-space. $FF ends the 18-row picture. The hand-over operands $0800/$DC00 are post-loop values, not the initial clear destinations.

Draw the three-row cyan message panel, print the inverse 40-character loading message from $0A50, set logical file2/device8/secondary3, and KERNAL LOAD the nine-character INTRO.SYS filename into $2000. SETMSG receives0 to suppress KERNAL status text. Duplicate LDA #3 at $089A/$089C is retained.

After LOAD, require $9FFF==0. On failure print the40-character error message from $0A28, scan keyboard until GETIN returns nonzero, then retry $0898. This checks the loaded sentinel, not KERNAL carry or a file checksum.
JMP $2F03 only after the zero sentinel test succeeds. entry.vsf is stopped at that destination before its first instruction; resident $2000-$9FFF matches INTRO.SYS exactly.
Nine PETSCII bytes INTRO.SYS supplied to SETNAM at $08CE. This is the single32KB resident image, distinct from later PLF level files.

Eighteen rows of16 color nibbles plus $FF terminator. Each value becomes two neighboring text cells; zero leaves a space, nonzero writes reverse-space. Expanded width32 cells; this is the colored illustration shown while INTRO.SYS loads.
Forty PETSCII characters displayed after nonzero $9FFF: disk-load error and press-any-key retry. Conversion AND $3F / OR $80 yields inverse screen codes.
Forty PETSCII characters displayed before LOAD: program load in progress, please wait. The loader copies backwards with Y=40..1 using base $0A4F.

392 remaining bytes of the fixed1024-byte loader file. They retain the alternating $00/$FF memory pattern with isolated changed bytes. The decoded loader refers only through $0A77 for code, text and picture; no role is assigned to this tail.
Authored 40-column high-score screen: four rows of borders, TOP SCORES and HIGH BONUS headings. The complete $2000-$23FF image is the SCORES disk file; $2403/$2800 copy it to $0400.

Twenty screen rows, 40 bytes each, hold two independent ranking lists. Left record begins $20A6, right $20BA; each is 12 bytes: three initials, space, six right-aligned decimal score characters, space, completion/mode marker. $24A8 compares digits and shifts records downward while leaving rank numbers and borders in place.
Bottom row of the two score-table frames. Insertion at $2546 redraws portions of this horizontal border after shifting the lowest records.
Last 24 bytes of the 1 KB SCORES image are outside the 1000 visible screen cells. Loaded fill (mostly 00/FF, with 2A at $23FC); save/load preserves it, but the ranking code does not parse it.
Public entry for game-over and completion ranking: jumps to $2553 to insert this player total and accumulated bonus, solicit initials when qualified, and show both lists.

Copy four pages $2000-$23FF to screen $0400-$07FF, colour all cells cyan (3), enable the text display, choose green border/black background, and install $2446 as the first IRQ work callback. Page operands are rewritten before the loop.
High byte of the colour-store operand at $2416; initialized $D8 and incremented once per 256-byte page while copying the score screen.
High byte of score source LDA$2419; starts $20 and advances through $23 during four-page screen copy.
High byte of screen destination STA$241C; starts $04 and advances through $07.

Every fourth $4020 tick, cycle a 16-colour palette and paint 16 cells in each qualified record row. $24A4/5 and $24A6/7 are score-image addresses; adding $B8 to their high bytes maps them into colour RAM. Nonqualification uses an out-of-screen sentinel.
Incrementing phase used by $2446, masked to sixteen palette entries.
Sixteen colour values for qualified rows: 1..7,1,8..15; black is omitted.
Descending rank search count, initialized to20. On insertion it is the number of rows from the chosen place through rank20; zero means no qualification.

Twelve-byte candidate record: three blank initials and separator, six digits from $554B at $249A-$249F, separator, and mode/completion screen code. Insertion strips bit7 from all bytes. Initials editor writes positions4..6 relative to its pointers after backing those pointers up by4.
Final byte of the 12-byte candidate; screen-code completion/mode letter chosen from $26CD[$40FB].
Current list base $20A6 (total) or $20BA (bonus), loaded into the self-modified compare at $24C0.
High byte of current score-list base, paired with $24A2; default $20 and unchanged for left/right lists.
Address returned for the total-score row; $FEFE means no row qualified. Before initials entry the pointer is decremented by4 for indexing positions4..6.
High byte of total-score insertion pointer $24A4/5; $FE in failure sentinel, or $20-$23 for an actual record.
Last insertion result, retained for the bonus list: selected record address or $FEFE sentinel. Also used by highlight and initials routines.
High byte of bonus-score insertion result $24A6/7; caller combines it with the total pointer high byte to detect double failure.

Compare candidate digits $249A-$249F lexicographically with20 records at the selected table base, stride40. Strictly greater chooses a position; equal scores continue downward. Failure returns $FEFE in $24A6/7. Success falls through to $24EB. Live native insertion checks:0 against zero table rejects;1 inserts first;100 ties below100;101 ranks above100.
Low-byte operand of CMP at $24C0. Initialized from current list base and advanced 40 bytes per rank during strict six-character comparison.
High-byte operand of CMP$24C0, incremented when the 40-byte rank stride crosses a page.

Shift lower12-byte records down40 bytes, working upward from the bottom using self-modified source/destination addresses initialized by $2553. Store candidate with inverse bit stripped, return insertion pointer at $24A6/7, repair bottom border, and return carry set.
Low-byte operand of LDA$24FB. Setup selects $76 for total or $8A for bonus at page $23; decrement by 40 while shifting records upward through the source list.
High byte of the self-modified shift-source LDA, reset $23 at insertion and decremented on 40-byte-stride borrow.
Low-byte operand of STA$24FE. Starts $9E/$B2 for total/bonus rank 20; decremented 40 with each shifted record and retained as insertion address.
High byte of self-modified shift-destination STA$24FE, initially $23; paired with $24FF and decremented on borrow.
Low-byte operand of candidate-write STA$253E, copied from final shift destination and also returned at $24A6.
High-byte operand of candidate-write STA$253E, also returned in $24A7.

Format and independently insert 24-bit total $40DA-DC and cumulative bonus $40DD-DF into two20-row lists. Failure returns $FEFE. If either qualifies, subtract4 from both destinations for initials. CPU checks bound failed-list glyph writes to underlying RAM $FEFE-$FF00/$E2FE-$E300 and highlight writes to old bitmap $B6FA-$B709 (both fail: $B6FE-$B70D). Vectors and mapped KERNAL reads stay unchanged; normal $447A clears the bitmap residue. Native100-point qualification with bonus0, joystick ABC entry and return/reboot passed.

Initialize alphabet index X=0 and first initials position Y=4, patch four store operands for both stored score records and their screen copies, then poll sound/fire state. Failed qualification leaves sentinel-derived pointers, which the four stores still write.
Write screen code $26D4[X] into both stored score records and both screen copies at offset Y; rejoin initials input loop. The two copies are separated by $1C00 between score image and screen.
Low-byte operand of first initials store $2634; points 4 bytes before the qualified total record so Y=4..6 addresses its three initials.
High byte of first initials record-store operand; retains sentinel-derived value when total score did not qualify.
Low-byte operand of second initials store $2637, matching total record low byte for the displayed copy.
High-byte operand of screen initials store $2637, score-image high byte minus $1C to map $2000 image to $0400 screen.
Low-byte operand of third initials store $263A for bonus-list record.
High byte of the bonus-record initials store; paired with $263B and potentially sentinel-derived.
Low-byte operand of fourth initials store $263D for bonus-list screen copy.
High-byte operand of bonus screen initials store $263D; stored-image high byte minus $1C.

Accept current initial and queue $26B8, priority=current Y4/5/6, release0, pulse control$40. LDX0 precedes the stack save, resetting the next alphabet selector. Advance Y;7 enters $268E. This path does not draw a glyph: untouched positions stay blank. Held fire can accept again when all sound priorities clear (25ticks for this cue), without a release-edge test. Native joystick ABC entry verified.

Use signed direction $4051 to move around the32-character alphabet (AND31). $26F4 starts at16 for repeat delay and decrements when $4021 advances. A direction of0 does nothing; updated choice is drawn by $2631.
After three initials, wait until counter $4022 reaches80, then call $2F00 to replace the SCORES file with the modified1KB table.
Queue tune14 through $4370/$6000, wait until all three sound-stream priorities $4032/$4039/$4040 are zero, disable first IRQ work callback by restoring RTS at $40C3, then return.

Initials confirmation sound stream: envelope AD=00/SR=50, then pulse widths $8888,$4444,$CCCC with frequency $433D held 8 ticks each. The zero terminator at $26CD is shared with the first completion-marker byte. Queued with release threshold 0 and pulse waveform $40.

Seven screen-code markers indexed by $40FB: 00,02,09,01,07,12,20 = @,B,I,A,G,R,space. Marks Beginner, Intermediate, Advanced, Grand Loop, Randomizer or an unfinished run according to caller-selected index.
Thirty-two selectable initials characters, in index order: ? / - * . Z through A, then space. Joystick changes index modulo32; fire confirms three characters.
Joystick initials editor delay counter, set16 on a changed letter and decremented using $4021.

Loaded filler between initials editor and score-display routine: repeated FF FF 00 00 pattern with isolated source-image residues. Identical at entry and play; no pointer table in these routines targets it.

Disable display, copy the saved1KB scores image to text screen, initialize colour RAM, then scroll a colour wave down it. Reveal screen after24 iterations and continue until the low/high wave counters bitwise-AND to2; return to attract caller.
Self-modified source-page operand of LDA$281A, initialized $20 and advanced four pages.
Self-modified screen-page operand of STA$281D, initialized $04 and advanced four pages.
High-byte operand of colour STA$2822, initialized $D8 and advanced with each copied page.
Move24 colour rows down one row, insert a new40-cell colour band from $28B3, and increment16-bit iteration count at $28B0/1. Uses $62-$65 as source/destination pointers.
Incrementing palette index masked to15 by $2859.
16-bit iteration count for attract high-score colour wave. Starts0; display turns on when low byte24, ends on the explicit low AND high ==2 test.
High byte of 16-bit colour-wave iteration count, incremented only when $28B0 wraps.
Rows still to shift in $2859, initialized24 each pass.
Sixteen colour values 1..15 then8, used as successive top-row colours in attract score display.
Loaded FF/00 filler after the16-entry colour palette and before $2900; unchanged between loader hand-over and gameplay.

Prepare EACH JUMPMAN X ... BONUS text, turn lives-minus-one $40E4 into a count, draw life markers, and select mode1..4 award100/250/500/750 from split table $29FF/$2A03. Clear award accumulator and show per-life multiplier.

For each remaining life, recolour its marker, add per-life award to $2A07/8, display running award, play $2A0C and pause48 ticks. Then wait for $4021 to wrap to0 and add award to both score totals at $2A1C. The displayed carry byte is written only to $40D7, not stored back to $2A09.
Forty-character final-life tally label, copied to the bottom screen row with inverse-video bit set: EACH JUMPMAN X ... --> BONUS ...0.
Low bytes of mode1..4 final-life awards: $64,$FA,$F4,$EE. Indexed through base $29FE plus $40FF.
High bytes paired with $29FF: 0,0,1,2, giving100,250,500,750 points per remaining life.
Three reserved bytes for completion award; loop updates the low two only, with transient carry displayed through $40D7. $2A1C adds the low16-bit total into both24-bit score records.
High byte of the 16-bit accumulated final-life award, updated by $298C-$2995 and added to both scores by $2A1C.
Reserved third byte, cleared at tally start but never updated; loop uses it to form a transient displayed carry and does not preserve carries beyond 16 bits.
Selected mode-dependent award per life, copied from split table before tally starts.
High byte of per-life award $2A0A/B,0/0/1/2 for modes 1..4.

Per-life bonus sound: envelope 22/42, pulse width $8888, then three descending frequency words $219F,$1930,$10CF held 6 ticks each, followed by 0. Queued with release threshold 1 and pulse control $40.
Add16-bit life bonus $2A07/8 to24-bit total $40DA-DC and accumulated bonus $40DD-DF, propagating carry to the third byte. Then enter mission-completed scene at $2A60.
Unreached loaded fragment before $2A60. Bytes49 43 are followed by a colour/platform-fill loop; the preceding JMP at $2A4C skips this fragment. No separate callable entry identified.

Reset display/sprites, draw a platform and MISSION COMPLETED / FINAL SCORE text, then stamp14 screen cells and colours using offset pairs $2AC8 and value pairs $2AE4. Continue into three-building renderer $2B83.

Fourteen little-endian offsets relative to $0400, also mapped to colour RAM by adding $D800. First10 mark star/light cells; last4 form roof/tile details. $2BBD chooses among the first10 for colour twinkles.
High-byte indexing view of interleaved screen offsets beginning $2AC8; renderer uses $2AC7+X with X=2..28.
Fourteen pairs of screen code and colour, matched to $2AC8 offsets. Ten dots and four green decorative character cells surround the completion buildings.
Eighteen-character MISSION COMPLETED! label, converted to screen codes by $2A80.
Eighteen-character FINAL SCORE 000000 template; $2BDB replaces the six zeroes with the24-bit total score.
Fifteen absolute colour-RAM pointers. Completion callback $2C00 writes each pointer and pointer+2 as a window pair; mode-specific subranges come from $2B42/$2B46.
High-byte indexing view of the 15 interleaved colour-RAM pointers at $2B24, fetched separately by $2C21.
First window-pair index for modes1..4:0,4,9,0. Indexed through $2B41 plus $40FF.
Exclusive window-pair endpoints for modes1..4:4,9,15,15. Grand Loop therefore flashes all three buildings.
Five split3-entry arrays: screen pointer lows43,FA,B1; highs06,05,05; colour pointer lows43,FA,B1; highsDA,D9,D9; heights8,10,12. $2B83 draws each as five inverse-space cells per row.
Three high bytes 06,05,05 paired with screen-pointer lows at $2B4A.
Three low bytes 43,FA,B1 of building colour-RAM starting addresses.
Three high bytesDA,D9,D9, paired with $2B50 colour-pointer lows.
Three heights 8,10,12, each building five character cells wide.
Current one-of-three building index used by $2B83.
Inputs $3B/3C screen pointer, $3D/3E colour pointer, X height. Fill five cells per row with inverse-space $A0 and blue6, advancing pointers40 bytes until X rows finish.
Read the five split arrays at $2B4A to draw5x8,5x10 and5x12 buildings; install star twinkle $2BBD in callback slot $40C8/9 then show the final score.
Take low random nibble from $4373; values0..9 select one of the first10 cell offsets and increment its colour RAM byte through a self-modified INC. Values10..15 leave the display unchanged.
Low-byte operand of twinkle INC$2BD7, selected from one of ten screen-cell offsets.
High-byte operand of twinkle INC$2BD7, offset high byte plus $D8 selects colour RAM.
Format $40DA-DC into screen at $07D7, install building-lights callback $2C00 in $40CA/CB, and enter actor setup $2C45.
Increment divider; only every16th call reaches the mode-specific building-window blink at $2C0D.
Frame divider and current window colour, toggled between black0 and yellow7 by $2C0D.
Current colour for mode-completed building windows; callback toggles 0/7 after writing selected pairs.
Select window-pair interval from mode $40FF and $2B42/$2B46, write current colour to each pair, then toggle0/7. Modes1,2,3 illuminate respectively4,5,6 pairs; Grand Loop uses all15.
Exclusive byte offset into the little-endian pointer list, equal to twice the selected end index.

Copy all2KB authored sprite data $8800-$8FFF down to $3000-$37FF, overwriting the active level overlay so text-bank sprite pointers can show the same artwork. Configure two sprites from $2C99-$2CA0, reveal scene and queue tune15 through $4370/$6000, then run the exit animation.
High-byte operand of LDA$2C54. Initialized $88 and advanced eight pages to copy all resident player/action sprites.
High-byte operand of STA$2C57. Initialized $30 and advanced eight pages, replacing the current level overlay with sprite art.
Four two-byte arrays: X positions48/46, Y216/50, sprite pointers$C3/$D9 in VIC bank0, colours2/12. Sprites reference the copied $3000 block.

Seven motion triples (dx,dy,duration), ending0,0,0. $2CB6 applies signed8-bit deltas to sprite1 at half-rate and advances its sprite pointer at each new triple; horizontal carry increments X-high even for negative deltas.
Vertical-delta indexing view of the triples at $2CA1, selected by byte offset $2D0B.
Duration indexing view of $2CA1 motion triples; zero marks the end and hides the completion actor.

On even $4020 ticks move sprite1 by active deltas $2D09/A for countdown $2D08; when empty read next triple at $2CA1+$2D0B and advance frame pointer $07F9. Zero duration hides sprite by setting its Y=0.
Motion countdown, horizontal delta, vertical delta, and triple-stream byte offset used by $2CB6.
Current 8-bit horizontal movement delta for completion sprite 1.
Current 8-bit vertical movement delta for completion sprite 1.
Byte offset into $2CA1 triples, advanced 3 per segment; main thread hides sprite 0 when this reaches 6.

Install motion callback $2CB6 in $40CC/CD, set sprite1 behind the background, hide sprite0 when script offset reaches6, and wait for sprite1 Y=0. Disable sprites, mark completion from $40FF into $40FB, enter high scores, set lives sentinel$FF, and return to turn manager $7400.
Loaded FF/00 patterned filler between completion animation and disk entry; identical at loader hand-over and first-level play, with no owned pointer/script targets.
Jump-vector entry to $2F84, which scratches the previous SCORES disk file and saves $2000-$23FF.

Entry from disk loader. Close logical file2, read one buffered PETSCII key: HOME$13 or CLEAR$93 chooses score reset; otherwise configure device8 secondary3, load six-character SCORES filename into $2000, close file2 and jump to $9000. Does not branch on LOAD error status.

Keep the default score-table image supplied by INTRO.SYS, print the40-character HIGH SCORES BEING CLEARED message on loading screen, save it through $2F00, then enter title initialization $9000. This is selected by buffered HOME or CLEAR at hand-over.
Isolated RTI byte after the startup jump. No caller found; preserve as authored entry-point-sized code rather than interpreting adjacent filenames as instructions.
Literal 0: preceding SCORES; filename calls point directly at $2F4D with length6, so this prefix is not passed to LOAD/SAVE.
Six-byte KERNAL filename SCORES for startup LOAD and persistent score SAVE.
Nine-byte drive command S0:SCORES, sent by OPEN on device8 command channel15 before replacement save.
Forty-character loading message ****** HIGH SCORES BEING CLEARED. ******, converted to inverse screen codes by $2F35.

OPEN logical file2/device8/secondary15 with S0:SCORES, close, set filename SCORES on secondary3, then KERNAL SAVE with start pointer $3D/3E=$2000 and end X/Y=$2400. Exactly1024 score bytes are written; close file2 and return without explicit status/error check. Live controlled SAVE then clearing1024 RAM bytes and native LOAD restored all1024 bytes exactly on the working disk; Natural100-point/ABC entry and menu return followed by hard reset and fresh native startup also restore all1024 saved bytes exactly.
Loaded repeated FF/00 filler after the disk save routine; no data, code or pointer target found in this tail.
Little-endian pointer to the level drawing command stream consumed by $4D0F. $FC commands replace it; callers choose geometry and bomb-erasure streams.
Drawing interpreter completion byte, cleared when $4D0F encounters $FF. No nonzero writer is established in the resident engine.
Byte offset of the next word in the IRQ task list. Advanced twice per dispatch and reset when the target high byte equals $EA.

Fourteen little-endian dispatch words read by $42DB. Initial tasks: keyboard$57C0, death$5C00, six empty$40C3 slots, movement$4900, hazards$6800, sprite upload$4600, terrain sampling$47C0, sound$44C0, then$EA31 sentinel. In play the sixth empty slot holds the overlay callback. Slots$400C-$4013 are replaced from$40C8-$40CF; $EA in a target high byte ends the list without calling it.
Eight-bit raster-service counter; wraps modulo256. Every eighth increment also advances $4047.
Frame counter incremented each raster service. Title and transition code reset/read it for waits; shared with the loader timing routines.
Frame counter incremented each raster service. Spawn/transition animation resets it and waits for one or more increments.
Alternates 0/1 on every serviced raster interrupt, independent of the player speed divider.
Two-state animation phase advanced on each player movement pulse; used for walking/climbing sound cadence and two-frame poses.
Four-state animation phase advanced on each player movement pulse; selects consecutive walk and ladder sprite shapes.
Incremented each IRQ only while $4027 is nonzero. Overflow invokes $57D9 to subtract100 bonus points.
Nonzero enables the 256-frame bonus countdown. Spawn sets1; death/completion/setup and a zero bonus stop it.
Player life/action state: zero permits movement,1 requests death processing,2 is the disabled/setup state. Movement and hazard callbacks gate on this byte.
Live player update divisor. Values1-8 select movement cadence; values>=9 suppress both player and hazard pulses. Spawn copies the selected speed $40E3 here.
Live second update divisor, tested against $40C2 to emit $402C. Spawn loads the selected speed into it; player switching preserves it in the speed field.
IRQ clears this pulse then sets1 when player divider expires. $4900 movement and overlay callbacks consume it.
IRQ clears this pulse then sets1 when the second divider expires. $6800 hazard update consumes it.
Sound scheduler increments this while changing voice records. The IRQ sound interpreter returns without processing voices while it is nonzero.
Little-endian sound bytecode pointer passed to $458E; caller also supplies A priority, X release threshold and Y SID control/waveform.

Three seven-byte records, one per SID voice: release threshold, remaining duration, priority (zero=idle), stream address low/high, control with gate cleared, spare byte. $44C0 steps records at offsets0,7,14; $458E allocates or preempts them.
Death-sequence sound latch. Reset by setup/spawn; $5C23 tests it before starting the falling/death sound and increments it once.
Death animation latch/state shared by $5C1D and $5D6D; setup/spawn clear it.
Incremented once per eight raster services. Its value is temporarily written to VIC interrupt-enable $D01A at $4209, then $413E restores $81. It is not a SID random-register read.
Indirect destination for RETURN escape: IRQ resets the CPU stack and jumps here when $404C is enabled and KERNAL keycode is1. Initialization sets $7800 (options).
Indirect destination for SPACE escape when $404D is enabled and keycode=$3C. The IRQ resets the CPU stack before jumping.
RETURN and SPACE escape enables, respectively; checked before the IRQ saves the banking port or dispatches game tasks.
Set when raster service changes to status-panel text. $42AD clears it after restoring multicolor bitmap mode outside raster lines50-250.
Nonzero keeps the raster handler from switching display modes. Text setup sets1; bitmap setup clears it for the status-panel split.
Signed horizontal and vertical intent from the16-pair lookup at $4320: -1,0,+1. These are intent values, not pixel velocities.
Active-low low nibble from joystick port2 ($DC00). A nonzero high nibble overrides real input and is mirrored down for scripted movement.
Bit4 holds active-low fire. Internal bit0 forces released ($11), bit1 forces pressed ($02); otherwise IRQ polls $DC00 bit4.
Five initialized resident bytes ($D9,$57,0,0,0), unchanged between loader hand-over and play. The first pair resembles $57D9 but the IRQ calls that routine directly; no reader is established.
X- and Y-expansion bitmasks copied every IRQ to $D01D/$D017. Setup clears both.
Eight software sprite enables. $4600 disables a hardware sprite and clears its cached X when its flag is zero; any nonzero value enables an active sprite.
Remaining seven software sprite enables (sprites1-7), following Jumpman at$405B. Zero disables the corresponding hardware sprite; level and hazard routines set nonzero to activate it.
Eight sprite X low bytes. Entry0 is Jumpman; $406B holds its high bit. Movement changes X by4 hardware pixels per step.
Eight sprite X high bytes, treated as boolean by the uploader and as carry/high byte by movement; hardware packs their bits in $D010.
Eight sprite Y positions. Entry0 is Jumpman; walking terrain, climbing, jumping and death routines modify it.
Eight VIC sprite shape indices, written to $83F8-$83FF by $4600. Shapes resolve as $8000+64*index in the bitmap VIC bank.
Shape indices for sprites1-7 after Jumpman slot0. The sprite uploader copies these to$83F9-$83FF; bank$8000 plus64*index locates each shape.
Five zero initialized bytes between sprite shape indices and collision snapshots. The indexed store based at $4087 uses X=8..1 and therefore starts at $4088, not here.
Eight per-sprite snapshots of hardware sprite-sprite collision. IRQ stores the complete $D01E mask for each sprite whose bit is set and zero for every other sprite.
Eight background-collision latches. For each bit set in $D01F, IRQ stores the complete mask; entries whose bit is clear retain their previous value.
OR of bitmap pixel-class flags across five sampled body rows:1 empty,2 collectible,4 support,8 climbable. Produced by $47C0, consumed by movement and bomb collection.
Saved $01 banking value. IRQ clears bit0 to expose bitmap RAM under BASIC, then restores the original value before its final acknowledgement.
Two zero initialized bytes between banking state and foot material flags; no reader or writer established.
OR of pixel-class flags in the foot strip sampled at $409D-$409F. Combined with body flags to test support and climbable geometry.
Foot probe X low/high and Y. Movement stores the current player X and sprite Y+11; the collision callback samples the bitmap at this position.
Last low X positions uploaded to VIC for each sprite. Cleared for disabled sprites; used to avoid redundant register writes.
Last Y positions uploaded to VIC, used to skip unchanged Y-register writes.
Eight multicolor-coordinate X columns populated from the level header. Ladder/up-rope entry accepts these columns or +/-2 and snaps to the center; lateral jump capture requires exact alignment.
Six exact multicolor-coordinate X columns used by the down-rope movement path. Matching climbable terrain at one adds2 to sprite Y automatically; $FF slots are inactive in level1.
Jump trajectory step,0 when grounded. $4B23 consumes22 trajectory pairs; from step7 onward support or aligned climbable contact can end it early.
Byte index into $4BFF trajectory pairs. Jump launch uses0 for vertical,$2C for right,$58 for left; each step adds2.

Set after one grounded update finds neither support nor climbable pixels and moves down2. A second unsupported grounded update requests death; landing clears it. Jumping uses separate trajectory logic.
Player and hazard counters. IRQ compares counter+1 with the corresponding speed; pulse occurs only when greater, resets counter to0, then increments to1.
One RTS shared by unused IRQ task slots. Pending callback updates can replace a live slot with this no-op.
Four zero initialized control bytes; $758F explicitly clears $40C7 during level setup. No consumer is established for this cleared byte.
Four little-endian pending callback vectors for slots $400C,$400E,$4010,$4012. A nonzero high byte commits the word during IRQ and clears that high-byte flag.
Five PETSCII filename bytes PLFxx. Progression changes the final two characters before loading the next2048-byte overlay.
Unsigned24-bit input/destructive remainder for $554B decimal conversion, loaded from total score or16-bit level bonus.
Little-endian six-character destination for $554B; score uses $07C8 and bonus $07E0.
Current player unsigned24-bit total score, little endian. Bomb awards, completion bonus and end-game life awards add here.
Current player unsigned24-bit accumulated bonus score, little endian. Completion bonus and end-game life awards add here; used for the separate HIGH BONUS records.
Unsigned24-bit next extra-life threshold, initially10000. $5E06 compares total score and advances the threshold by10000 after awarding a life.
Player selected speed1-8. Keyboard changes this byte immediately; spawn copies it to live dividers $4029/$402A. Part of the11-byte saved player record.
Lives minus one: initial6 means7 displayed lives; death decrements, and $FF marks elimination. HUD adds1; extra-life code increments this byte.
Set by roster scan when no configured player retains a life; zero while at least one saved player record is active.
Set when next-player selection wraps to player1; transition code uses it to decide when to advance the shared level.
Debounce keycode for speed selection; $40 denotes no key. Repeated held keys do not rewrite the selection.
